Portable contracts distinguish adapter obligations from SQLite implementation proof; future authentication/backend parity stays unproven. goalAtSelection:
Prove and strengthen Tracer’s existing engineering workflows under concurrent independent local clients/processes and realistic project workloads. Preserve the verified primitives, application contracts and existing configuration/assessment/verification meaning.

First inspect the live register, repository and transaction contracts, existing concurrency/recovery tests, real Tracer project and benchmark evidence. Refine WORK-006 into concrete local proof, preserving REQ-025’s separate future authenticated-team/backend obligation. Register a bounded requirement, method, workload profiles, failure cases and measurable acceptance before implementation. Do not infer multiuser or scale readiness from single-process queues or synthetic counts alone.

Demonstrate concurrent native/schema/link/resource operations and atomic native-plus-evidence application commands from independent repository instances and operating-system processes. Prove conflict/stale guards, unique identities, original-intent outcomes, immutable ordered history, complete rollback and usable recovery after failed transactions. Exercise identical/conflicting command IDs, schema/data races, endpoint deletion/relinking and genuinely concurrent assessment/verification operations. Never lose an acknowledged update, publish partial state, duplicate successful outcomes or automatically replay an uncertain write.

Verify consistent reads during concurrent writes, including their declared snapshot and pagination guarantees. Preserve exact configuration comparison and candidate applicability independently of unrelated head changes. Explicitly reject stale continuation/guard contexts where promised; do not claim cross-request snapshot isolation where absent.

Prove restart, lost committed-response inspection, crash/interruption recovery and SQLite-aware online backup/restoration while work is active. Recover exact original outcomes and preserve native/evidence history and the two controlled engineering application capabilities.

Establish reproducible workloads from the actual Tracer project plus justified connected synthetic engineering/research profiles. Measure latency, memory, query/payload/work bounds and contention; declare budgets from task evidence and initial baseline before optimization. Fix demonstrated correctness and material performance/maintainability problems through existing owners and portable repository contracts; avoid speculative frameworks, silent truncation, weakened gates or replacing complete engineering scope with an easier subset.

Execute the declared core/typed HTTP/client/CLI and relevant shared-workspace tasks, success/rejection/recovery and boundary cases. Retain exact candidate/procedure/results, environment, workloads, uncertainty and measured limits. Pass appropriate regression, architecture and quality gates unchanged. Update owning architecture/usage docs, checkpoint and guarded register; export and verify online/restored backup preservation. Audit every criterion and the full objective before completion.

Exclude organizational authentication/permissions, hosting, second database adapters, cloud integrations and arbitrary-scale or representative-human readiness claims. A future adapter must satisfy the strengthened portable contract; this goal does not claim parity with an unimplemented backend. Success is correct, recoverable and measured responsive operation for explicitly declared local concurrent workloads, with independent process evidence rather than promise.
limits: Read-only drivers inspect the existing backed-up live project and use fresh temporary restore paths. Never silently reseed a missing database; inspect exact durable original outcomes before any deliberate new mutation. Review export alone is not restorable.
